label: Weak, dense hum that rises when text is about treating or caring for mental illness (psychiatric nurses and wards, antipsychotics, antidepressants, ECT, eating-disorder clinics, asylums, crisis teams), even without the words 'psychiatry' or 'therapy'; the same care scenes for physical illness (knees, measles, TB, cancer, diabetes, asthma) stay lower (~0.1-0.25), and mental distress told in plain words without any care setting (panic, grief, hopelessness) also stays near the hum (~0.15-0.2). Side channels from earlier tests still apply: the '-therapy' word family off-topic (speech therapy ~0.46) and the 'Too Little too Late?' headline. Its mapped neighbours (Texas names, shorthand text, re-typed strings) share no topic with it, so they do not change the label.

qc.label_under_test: Weak, dense hum that rises on mental-health care and psychiatry in general, not only talking therapy: psychiatrist/psychologist, psychiatric hospital, antidepressant prescriptions, ECT, hallucinations / hearing voices, clinical, bipolar and postnatal depression (about 0.3-0.65). Physical-medicine twins (cardiology, burns, chemotherapy, fractures, infections) stay lower (0.1-0.3). Side channels: the '-therapist/therapy' word family lifts it even off-topic (physiotherapist 0.35, speech therapy 0.46), and the 'Too Little too Late?' headline; some disorder names alone (OCD, PTSD, anorexia, delusions) stay near the hum (0.13-0.22).
